narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Direct writes in linked git worktrees are gated against the **primary checkout's** occupancy lease. The hook selects its project root from the payload's workspace fields and never consults where the write actually lands, so two isolated worktrees falsely contend and a parent can block its own child.

The lease files are correctly separate. The root selection is wrong.

Observed live on 2026-08-27 while independent tasks worked on #3609 and #3610.

## Root cause

`hookPayloadRootCandidates()` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:432-447`) offers only `workspaceRoot`, `workspace_root`, `workspace_roots[]`, and `cwd`. `projectRootFromHookPayload()` (`:476-487`) takes the first usable one. Neither inspects the write target or the Git worktree containing it.

The deposited hook supplies no `--project-root` (`init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts:83`), so `hook-dispatch.ts:201-202` always resolves from the payload. `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` then reads `<projectRoot>/.deft/occupancy.json` (`occupancy.ts:79-81`).

The information needed is already in hand: `hookWriteTargetPath(input.payload)` is called at `dispatcher.ts:937`, 74 lines before the occupancy gate at `:1011`. `worktreePath()` exists at `session/git.ts:154`.

## Scope correction: this is a direct-write defect

**Occupancy gates exactly one tool family today: direct writes.** Shell reaches `inspectMutationGates` only via `decideShellDestFormsThenRuntimeAuthority` (`:1310`), which requires `shellDestForms === "enforce"`; the default is `"off"` (`runtime-authority.ts:73`) and this repo does not set it. Spawn is exempt at `:1009`. MCP never arrives.

**The "nested execution directory for lifecycle commands" limb has been removed** from the remedy. No supported host sends one on a shell payload -- all six Shell fixtures in `hooks/fixtures/cases.ts` carry only `tool_input.command`, and where Cursor does send `cwd` it equals `workspace_roots`, the wrong root already. `lifecycleExecutionRootCheck` reports `aligned: true` when the fields are absent, so the limb would inherit a check that passes by default on missing input.

## Remedy

Two named roots, not one swap.

**`payloadRoot`** stays as today and remains authoritative for: authz grant scoping (`:780`, exact-string matched at `authz/evaluate.ts:124-126` -- re-pointing breaks every live UAT grant), the authz audit trail (`:686`, which would otherwise shard one repository-global evidence file into per-worktree files deleted with their worktree), the `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch (`:1545-1551`, untracked and therefore absent from linked worktrees), the #2885 outside-root carve-out, and `deny()`.

**`effectiveRoot`** is resolved once from the Git toplevel of the nearest **existing** ancestor of the write target, through the memoized runner at `:931`, and is admitted **only when** its `rev-parse --git-common-dir` matches `payloadRoot`'s. It governs occupancy and ritual.

That single `--git-common-dir` comparison is simultaneously the linked-worktree admission test, the foreign-repository refusal, and the cross-worktree detector.

## Acceptance -- commit 1

- [ ] A direct write is gated against the Git worktree containing its target
- [ ] `effectiveRoot` is admitted only when `--git-common-dir` matches `payloadRoot`'s; otherwise fall back to `payloadRoot`
- [ ] **Occupancy and ritual move together in this commit** -- see the atomic-seam note below
- [ ] Authz grant scoping, the authz audit trail, and the kill-switch are **explicitly pinned** to `payloadRoot`
- [ ] A resolver that returns `string | null` replaces bare `worktreePath()` for this path, with a walk-up to the nearest existing ancestor before spawning
- [ ] Git output is normalised through `normalizeHookProjectRoot` before comparison
- [ ] Both roots appear in every deny message, so an operator can see which tree was judged
- [ ] A foreign-repository target is refused rather than adopted
- [ ] Integration regression: one primary repo plus two real linked worktrees, invoking the deposited hook CLI without `--project-root`
- [ ] Allow/deny matrix pinned: unrelated primary lease does not block; foreign target-worktree lease denies; matching target-worktree lease allows
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

## Acceptance -- commit 2, deliberate and separate

- [ ] Active scope and `file_scope` relativization move to `effectiveRoot`
- [ ] The assist-scratch reclassification lands with a named migration note -- see below

## Constraints established by the round-1 panel

Synthesis 5434084528; deposits 5434003949, 5434012950, 5434038821.

**Occupancy and ritual are one atomic seam.** They are cross-compared at `:1058-1087` and `:1139-1151`. Moving one without the other reads the worker's lease from the worktree and the parent's ritual owner from the primary; those never match, and every worktree write then denies `occupancy-ritual-mismatch` with remediation no single `session:start` can satisfy, because `.deft/` is gitignored and the two files live in different trees. That state is strictly worse than today, where the failure is at least actionable.

**Commit 1 must contain the containment test.** Measured: `isOutsideProjectRootWrite(worktree, primaryFile)` is `true`, and `:1201-1202` skips the entire scope deny for outside-root writes. Re-pointing the root without a cross-worktree detector makes cross-worktree writes *less* gated than they are now.

**Unconstrained target resolution is an authority-selection primitive.** `worktreePath()` has no containment check, so an absolute path into another repository on the same disk relocates occupancy, ritual, runtime authority, active scope, and the audit trail into that repository. The file path is attacker-influenceable.

**`worktreePath()` cannot express failure.** It returns `resolve(projectRoot)` on any non-zero exit, and a nonexistent `cwd` is reported as "git executable not found on PATH". A write creating a file in a not-yet-existing directory is the common case, so the resolver would silently fall back to the wrong root with no signal.

**An ambiguity denial must name both concrete roots.** `lifecycleExecutionRootCheck` currently denies with "Run the lifecycle command from the hook project root" without naming it, and for a genuine two-worktree span no single directory satisfies that instruction.

## Unbudgeted consequence: the assist-scratch bypass collapses

Swarm worktrees are created under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/` (`swarm/launch.ts:673`), and `.deft-scratch/` is an assist-scratch prefix (`:338`). Measured: **every file in every linked worktree is currently an allowlisted assist-scratch path**, so under assist or ephemeral posture those writes return `write-assist-scratch-ready` at `:950-963` and skip ritual, occupancy, and scope entirely.

Re-pointing closes that channel. That is the correct outcome and a new denial class for every assist-posture worktree agent, compounding with the ritual seam above. It also suggests that placing real product worktrees under a scratch-path fence deserves its own issue.

## Cost

Git spawn measured at **37ms** unloaded and serial on this host, against the 2.2s p50 recorded in #3737 under N-agent load. Both are correct; the marginal spawn is cheap at rest and expensive exactly when a swarm is running. The existing memoizer keys on the selected root (`git.ts:100`), so resolving the target's directory is a guaranteed miss -- one extra spawn per gated direct write if the resolver sits inside `inspectMutationGates`, more if it sits at the CLI entry. Put it inside the dispatch.

## Correction to a related issue

The original body inherited a claim that #3779's ordering makes the occupancy denial's printed remedy unrunnable. **At default policy it does not.** `occupancy:steal` and `occupancy:release` arrive as Shell, match none of the four dest-forms (`dest-form.ts:24`), never enter `inspectMutationGates`, and reach `inspectExactLifecycleCommand` (`:1433`) where both verbs are recognised. **#3779 needs re-derivation.**

## Related

- #3613 -- occupancy tracker; this is the root-routing dimension
- #3433 -- established the worktree-scoped lease contract this defect violates
- #3599 -- lease semantics. No collision: this changes *which* lease file is read, not what a lease means. It does multiply live lease files by the number of worktrees, which changes the population an age cap operates on.
- #3611 (closed) -- host-session identity. The enforcing binary is still `0.107.0`, so that fix is not yet live; it is an amplifier here, not the cause.
- #3779 -- see the correction above
- #3742 -- hook reachability and delivery

Refs #3613, #3433, #3599, #3611, #3779, #3742, #2885, #3039.

## Triage

mechanism-shaped: true

design-critique: warranted, though not because the diagnosis is doubtful. I re-verified all four code claims and they hold exactly. What warrants a panel is **blast radius**: the effective hook root underpins every gate the dispatcher applies -- occupancy, ritual, scope, runtime-authority, audit -- so changing how it is selected changes the frame of reference for all of them at once. Getting it wrong does not degrade one gate, it misaims the whole enforcement surface.

refutation-target: resolving the effective hook root from the direct-write target's Git toplevel, or from the nested execution directory for lifecycle commands, corrects the defect without breaking the gates that currently depend on the workspace root.

## What I verified before filing this write-back

All four root-cause claims confirmed at `e2b62217`:

```439:445:packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts
  push(input.workspaceRoot);
  push(input.workspace_root);
  const workspaceRoots = input.workspace_roots;
  if (Array.isArray(workspaceRoots)) {
    for (const entry of workspaceRoots) push(entry);
  }
  push(input.cwd);
```

`projectRootFromHookPayload` (`:476-487`) takes the first usable candidate; `worktreePath()` exists at `session/git.ts:154` backed by `rev-parse --show-toplevel`; occupancy resolves `<projectRoot>/.deft/occupancy.json`.

**The issue undersells itself in one respect.** `hookWriteTargetPath(input.payload)` is already called at `dispatcher.ts:616` -- a few lines *after* the wrong root is chosen -- and used only to compute a path relative to that wrong root. The information the fix needs is already in hand, so the core correction is a reordering rather than new plumbing. That makes it smaller than the acceptance list implies.

The same line is a concrete instance of the "misbinds scope" impact: a worktree write has its relative path computed against the primary root, yielding `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<w>/packages/...` where the gate expects `packages/...`.

**Version claim confirmed.** The installed global CLI here is also `0.107.0`, so #3611's fix -- merged today as `8f5dd900` -- is not in the enforcing binary. The amplifier described is live right now.

**Corroboration from the parent's own session.** I released the primary checkout's lease repeatedly today to unblock work, and attributed all of it to #3611. My workers were in linked worktrees under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/`, so their writes would have been evaluated against the primary lease I was holding. I cannot cleanly separate the two retrospectively, and I am not claiming I can -- but the reported pattern matches what I saw, and I would stop attributing it solely to #3611.

## Audit markers

- `audit:shell-path` -- a direct write has a target; a shell command may not. The remedy says "the nested execution directory for lifecycle commands", but establish whether the payload actually carries one on each supported host, and what happens when it does not. Shell is the highest-traffic gated tool. If the remedy only covers direct writes, it fixes the minority path and the parent-blocks-child failure persists for `Bash` / `Shell`.

- `audit:dependents` -- enumerate everything that currently consumes the selected root and determine whether any consumer *depends on it being the workspace root*. Occupancy and scope plainly want the worktree. Ritual, runtime-authority, and audit may not. If some gate is meant to be repository-global, silently re-pointing it at a worktree is a new defect, not a fix.

- `audit:ambiguity-remedy` -- acceptance criterion 3 adds a fail-closed path for ambiguous or cross-worktree invocations. That is a new denial. Apply today's lesson: can the blocked actor perform the remediation the denial prints? The occupancy denial already fails this test (#3779), and the #3599 age-cap fix nearly shipped the same trap. Establish that this one does not.

- `audit:split` -- acceptance criterion 2 asks for one resolver used consistently across five subsystems. That is a migration bundled with a targeted fix. Determine the **minimal correct first change** and whether the rollout is separable, or whether partial adoption creates a worse mixed state where two gates disagree about which tree they are protecting.

## Sequencing

#3599 is in flight against `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` (lease semantics: age cap, refresh discrimination). This issue changes *which* occupancy file is read rather than what the lease means, so they should compose -- but both land in the same neighbourhood and the panel should flag any collision it sees.

## Scope

Filed by @dbcall2 under #3613 as a new **root-routing** dimension. I agree it is not a duplicate: #3755 is same-worktree lineage semantics, #3599 is heartbeat expiry, #3729 is absent-lease admission, #3611 is host identity. None of them is about selecting the wrong tree. It restores the contract #3433 established rather than changing it.

## Ceiling and verdict

Input ceiling: issue body plus comments through and including `5433968047`.

I observed that the REST response also contained later comment `5433969633`. I excluded it completely from this critique.

**BROKEN.** Target-derived worktree resolution is the right direction for a scalar direct write, but the proposed one-root remedy cannot bind as written. It has no complete target set for multi-target tools, no reliable execution directory on any of the three supported-host lifecycle fixtures, and no distinction between a mutation worktree root and the workspace/control root used by non-mutation events.

## Finding 1 — `audit:shell-path`: the payload contract does not supply the proposed lifecycle root

**blocks-the-design**

**Evidence.** The Codex lifecycle fixtures carry a command but no execution-directory field (`packages/core/src/hooks/fixtures/cases.ts:589-674`). The Cursor lifecycle fixture likewise has no directory (`packages/core/src/hooks/fixtures/cases.ts:677-693`), as do both Claude lifecycle fixtures (`packages/core/src/hooks/fixtures/cases.ts:696-728`). The dispatcher looks for top-level or nested `cwd`, `workdir`, `working_directory`, and `workingDirectory` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1346-1373`), but if none is present it falls through to `aligned: true` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1416-1418`). The documented contract explicitly permits the shell execution directory to be absent (`content/commands.md:415`).

The audit premise that all Bash/Shell calls traverse the same mutation stack is not true in this tree. Shell is routed separately (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1753-1758`). Only opt-in recognized destination forms enter `inspectMutationGates` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1308-1335`), and that option defaults off (`packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts:67-74`). Other unclassified shell commands fail open (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:881-893`). Exact lifecycle commands receive identity/alignment handling only after the shell decision allows (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1426-1434`, `1756-1758`).

**Failure mode.** “Resolve from the nested execution directory” cannot execute when the host omits that field. Treating absence as workspace-root alignment repeats the current defect; treating absence as ambiguous introduces a denial for every current lifecycle fixture.

**Disposition consequence.** The remedy must not claim host-complete lifecycle resolution until Cursor, Claude, and Codex each have a measured payload contract and an explicit missing-directory policy. A first ship may preserve absent-field compatibility while correcting target-bearing writes, but that is narrower than acceptance criterion 1.

## Finding 2 — the direct-write “target” is not a complete mutation set

**blocks-the-design**

**Evidence.** The direct-write surface includes `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`, and `ApplyPatch` (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts:1-15`). Yet `hookWriteTargetPath` extracts one scalar from only `file_path`, `filePath`, or `path` (`packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts:8-23`). Even `hookPathSet` merely wraps that scalar and does not inspect `edits`, cells, or patch members (`packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts:56-69`). The classifier recognizes `toolInput.edits` as `MultiEdit` and cells as `NotebookEdit` (`packages/core/src/hooks/classify/tool-name.ts:48-51`) without supplying their target set.

**Failure mode.** A multi-edit can name files in two worktrees while the resolver sees zero or one target. It can select one lease/scope/policy root and authorize an operation that also mutates another tree, defeating acceptance criterion 3.

**Disposition consequence.** Replace the scalar premise with a complete, host-specific target-set extractor. Resolve every member to a Git toplevel; continue only when the set has exactly one root. Until extraction is complete for a tool, fail closed for that tool or leave it on the existing route—do not represent partial extraction as cross-worktree protection.

## Finding 3 — `audit:ambiguity-remedy`: an early root denial needs an out-of-band recovery

**blocks-the-design**

**Evidence.** Lifecycle inspection/rewrite runs only after the prior shell decision is `allow` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1431-1434`). A recognized shell destination-form denial returns before that attachment (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1326-1334`). Occupancy denial text recommends lifecycle actions (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:99-111`), while direct mutation occupancy denials return from `inspectMutationGates` before later shell lifecycle attachment (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1011-1056`, `1426-1434`).

The current-tree ordering is subtler than the parent claim: an exact bare `occupancy:release` is ordinarily an unclassifiable shell command, so it does not enter the direct-write occupancy branch. But a new effective-root ambiguity check placed before route selection would deny both the original mutation and the lifecycle command before that distinction can help.

**Failure mode.** The denied actor is told to run a command whose hook cannot select a root, producing the same denial again. For missing-directory hosts, the actor cannot add a payload field the host does not expose.

**Disposition consequence.** Either reserve a narrowly parsed exact lifecycle form with an explicit absolute `--project-root` and matching explicit owner before ambiguity denial, or direct the operator to an external terminal invocation. Add a regression that starts from the denial and proves the printed recovery succeeds.

## Finding 4 — `audit:dependents`: mutation consumers want the worktree, but `decideHook` also has control-root consumers

**sharpens-framing**

**Evidence and inventory.**

- **Occupancy: re-point.** It is explicitly a worktree lease and stores under `<root>/.deft/occupancy.json` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:1-14`, `27-30`, `79-81`).
- **Ritual: re-point.** State is below the supplied root and carries required `worktree_path` (`packages/core/src/session/ritual-sentinel.ts:17-18`, `31-38`, `53-55`, `84-98`). Verification compares it with Git toplevel (`packages/core/src/session/verify-session-ritual.ts:307-316`).
- **Scope/story fence: re-point.** Active scope is enumerated below the supplied root (`packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts:17-25`); the contract names host/worktree active-story identification as the seam (`content/contracts/path-write-fence.md:45-52`).
- **Runtime authority: re-point for target-bearing mutation.** Policy loads from that root’s PROJECT-DEFINITION (`packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts:223-226`), and paths are project-relative (`content/contracts/runtime-authority.md:16-27`).
- **Authz and audit: re-point together.** Grants bind `worktree` (`content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md:34-41`); evaluation rejects mismatch (`packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts:114-127`); state/grants/audit live below the supplied root (`packages/core/src/authz/paths.ts:4-22`); dispatcher passes that root as attempted worktree (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:762-782`).
- **Assist/proposed/outside-root: re-point.** All relativize the target against `projectRoot` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:323-330`, `937-949`, `1155-1169`, `1193-1202`).
- **Session start/compact and kill-switch: preserve control/workspace semantics unless separately designed.** Kill-switch runs before tool classification (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1537-1567`), compact mutates state from the incoming root (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1571-1610`), and SessionStart bookkeeping uses it (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1614-1678`). These events have no write target.
- **Spawn: preserve its route.** Spawn has no target and deliberately bypasses occupancy while using ritual/scope (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1008-1015`, `1712-1750`).

**Failure mode.** Replacing `input.projectRoot` globally changes session/compact/kill-switch/spawn behavior; re-pointing only occupancy creates a mixed lease/ritual/scope/authz/policy state.

**Disposition consequence.** Name two concepts: `workspaceRoot` and route-local `effectiveMutationRoot`. Within a target-bearing mutation, all mutation consumers switch atomically. Non-target events and spawn remain unchanged pending separate design.

## Finding 5 — `audit:split`: split by route, never by gate

**sharpens-framing**

**Evidence.** `inspectMutationGates` creates one Git memoizer and feeds one root to ritual, occupancy, scope, authz, runtime authority, and final occupancy recheck (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:923-932`, `967-1015`, `1113-1152`, `1187-1272`). It compares occupancy with the ritual’s bound owner (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1058-1086`).

**Failure mode.** Occupancy-only adoption can admit the target lease then reject the workspace ritual, or authorize against workspace story/policy while writing the target tree.

**Disposition consequence.** Rollout is separable only by tool route: (1) complete-target direct writes and proven opt-in shell dest forms atomically use `effectiveMutationRoot`; (2) exact lifecycle commands add host-measured directory support plus missing-field recovery; (3) ordinary shell/MCP, spawn, SessionStart, and compact remain unchanged.

## Cross-worktree orchestration, nesting, cost, and sequencing

**sharpens-framing**

**Ordinary orchestration.** One operation targeting one child worktree is not “cross-worktree” merely because the host workspace is primary. It uses the child root and must satisfy child state. Codex parent/subagents share an owner, Claude uses the session family, and Cursor uses the conversation owner (`packages/core/src/hooks/fixtures/README.md:24-35`), so same-family parent/child operation need not falsely contend. A genuinely multi-root operation denies.

**Nested worktrees.** I measured `git -C C:\Repos\deft\directive\.deft-scratch\worktrees\b3599\packages\core rev-parse --show-toplevel`; it returned the linked worktree, not primary. Git discovery disambiguates nesting. With target root selected, `isOutsideProjectRootWrite` treats a target inside it as inside (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:292-317`).

**Cost.** `worktreePath` spawns `rev-parse --show-toplevel` (`packages/core/src/session/git.ts:154-160`). #3736 can coalesce HEAD/toplevel/branch and cache within one dispatch (`packages/core/src/session/git.ts:50-68`, `88-137`), but its memoizer is created after root selection (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:923-932`). Lift and share it or resolution adds another spawn. A hook is a new CLI process, so this does not cache across tool calls. At measured ~2.2s p50, benchmark a nearest-existing-parent/`.git` fast path or accept one shared probe; do not add a resolver spawn plus existing gate spawns.

**Sequencing with #3599.** No direct semantic conflict: #3599 changes lease age/refresh in `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`; this changes which root reaches that API from `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`. Tests/release order may collide, but responsibilities compose.

## Injection / swarm lens

The payload is untrusted cooperative input and this changes identity, concurrency, worktrees, and shared state. Canonicalize/realpath the nearest existing ancestor before Git, reject incomplete target sets, and ensure resolved roots belong to the intended repository/worktree set. Lexical containment is insufficient under symlinks/junctions and `..`; the existing outside-root guard realpath-walks ancestors (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:287-317`). Owner equality still does not authorize one operation across two roots: root-set cardinality is the deterministic boundary.

## Minimal correct first change

Introduce route-local `effectiveMutationRoot` for target-bearing direct writes: extract the complete target set; resolve every target from a defined base to Git toplevel using one shared per-dispatch runner; require exactly one canonical root; then run the complete `inspectMutationGates` stack on that root. Leave session/compact/spawn/ordinary-shell roots unchanged. This is the smallest safe correction. Occupancy-only adoption is unsafe; global replacement is overbroad; lifecycle cwd resolution follows only after each host’s measured shape and missing-field recovery are pinned.

## Road not taken and steelman

I rejected “change only occupancy lookup.” It creates a lease/ritual/scope/authz split.

The strongest case for one resolver is that every target-bearing mutation consumer is worktree-relative, and one root removes accidental disagreement. I would flip to **SURVIVED** if the contract uses a complete target set, distinguishes control from mutation root, pins measured lifecycle-directory and missing-field behavior for all three hosts, proves the ambiguity recovery from the denied state, and holds Git cost to one shared/coalesced probe.

Note the side effect: today a worktree worker rides the **parent's** ritual, because the hook hands ritual the primary root and the primary's state self-consistently validates. After the move, the worker's own ceremony becomes authoritative -- correct, and a new denial for workers that never ran `session:start` in their worktree.

The `file_scope` fence expects the latter.

**Must NOT be silently re-pointed:**

- **Authz grant scoping.** `dispatcher.ts:780` passes `worktree: projectRoot` into `evaluateAuthzMutation`, and `authz/evaluate.ts:124-126` requires exact string equality against the grant's `worktree`. A human-origin grant issued against the primary root stops matching the moment the root becomes a worktree, producing `authz-grant-scope-deny` for every worker in an active UAT campaign. **Neutral but load-bearing for diagnosis:** `deny()` at `:512-529` stamps `projectRoot: resolve(input.projectRoot)` -- the *original*. If the effective root is computed inside `inspectMutationGates` and never written back, every deny message reports a root the gate did not actually use. Name both roots explicitly.

### 6. `sharpens-framing` -- re-pointing collapses an existing bypass, which is a bigger behavior change than AC3 describes

**Evidence.** Measured:

```
isAllowlistedAssistScratchPath(P, W\packages\core\src\session\occupancy.ts) = true
isAllowlistedAssistScratchPath(W, W\packages\core\src\session\occupancy.ts) = false
```

`ASSIST_SCRATCH_ROOT_PREFIXES` is `[".deft-scratch/", "temp/"]` (`:338`), and swarm worktrees are created at `join(projectRoot, ".deft-scratch", "worktrees", <id>)` (`swarm/launch.ts:673`). So **every file in every linked worktree is currently an allowlisted assist-scratch path.** Under assist or ephemeral posture, `isAssistScratchWrite` (`:412-423`) is satisfied and `inspectMutationGates` returns `write-assist-scratch-ready` at `:950-963`, before the ritual block at `:967` and before occupancy at `:1011`. Those writes skip ritual, occupancy, and scope entirely -- while the allow message at `:960-961` warns "do not smuggle source under `.deft-scratch/`".

**Failure mode.** The remedy closes that channel: after re-pointing, worktree files are no longer scratch-classified, and every assist/ephemeral worktree agent that writes source is newly subject to the full gate stack. This is the right outcome, but it is a denial class nobody has budgeted for, and it interacts with finding 2 -- these agents typically have no worktree-local ritual.

**Disposition consequence.** Land this deliberately with a named migration note, not as a side effect. It also argues that the placement of swarm worktrees under `.deft-scratch/` is itself worth a separate issue: a path fence for disposable notes is currently aliasing real product source.

### 7. `sharpens-framing` -- the ambiguity denial can be made recoverable, and the inherited #3779 ordering claim does not hold at the default policy

`audit:ambiguity-remedy`.

**Evidence.** The brief asserts that the occupancy deny at `:1028-1045` returns before `inspectExactLifecycleCommand` at `:1419`, so a denied party cannot run the printed `occupancy:steal` / `occupancy:release`. Traced at `e2b62217`, the ordering is real but the path is not reachable for the remediation command. `occupancy:steal` and `occupancy:release` arrive as **Shell**. Shell routes through `decideShellDestFormsThenRuntimeAuthority` (`:1757`), which touches `inspectMutationGates` only under `shellDestForms: "enforce"` (`:1308-1310`, default `"off"`) and only for a classified product dest-form -- and `dest-form.ts:24` recognizes exactly `git-checkout`, `git-restore`, `rm`, `rmdir`. A `deft occupancy:steal` invocation matches none of them. It reaches `attachLifecycleIdentityRewrite` (`:1758`) and `inspectExactLifecycleCommand` (`:1433`), where `occupancy:steal` and `occupancy:release` are both in `EXACT_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (`host-session-identity.ts:169-176`).

So the recovery command is not blocked by the occupancy gate. #3779 is a real issue -- I did not audit its actual mechanism, only the ordering claim as transcribed into this envelope -- but that specific ordering does not establish the trap here, and a new AC3 denial does not automatically inherit it.

**Where the new denial *would* be unusable.** `attachLifecycleIdentityRewrite` calls `lifecycleExecutionRootCheck(input.payload, input.projectRoot, ...)` at `:1489-1494` and denies `occupancy-identity-conflict` when the execution directory disagrees with the hook root, printing "Run the lifecycle command from the hook project root" (`:1500-1502`). If AC1 moves the hook root to the write target's worktree while the operator's shell sits in the primary, that message tells the operator to `cd` somewhere the message does not name -- and if the ambiguity is *between* two worktrees, there is no single directory that satisfies it.

**Disposition consequence.** The AC3 denial is recoverable **only if** its message names the concrete resolved root, the conflicting root, and a directory the actor can actually stand in. Require the deny text to interpolate both paths. A generic "the effective root is ambiguous" string reproduces the #3779 failure class by a different route.

### 8. `sharpens-framing` -- the cost objection is weaker than stated, but `worktreePath()` cannot express the failure AC3 needs

**Method-reconciliation first.** The brief cites a 2.2s p50 per `git.exe` spawn, sourced from #3736 (`git.ts:88-96` records the same figure). I measured five sequential `git -C .deft-scratch\worktrees\b3599 rev-parse --show-toplevel` invocations on this host at 184ms total, **37ms each**. I am not calling 2.2s false. #3736's figure is explicitly a loaded-box, N-concurrent-agents measurement; mine is unloaded and serial. Different method, so this is a discrepancy to explain: the marginal spawn costs 37ms when the box is idle and can cost far more under a live swarm, which is exactly when it matters.

**What the memoizer does and does not cover.** `memoizeGitRunner` (`git.ts:97-138`) caches `["rev-parse","--show-toplevel"]` and coalesces it with HEAD and branch into one child (`git.ts:55-61`, `:102-117`). The dispatch already pays that spawn, because `verifySessionRitual` calls `worktreePath` at `verify-session-ritual.ts:311` through the memoized runner built at `dispatcher.ts:931`. But the cache key is `[resolve(projectRoot), args]` (`git.ts:100`, `:120`), so resolving the toplevel of a *different* directory -- the write target's parent -- is a cache miss by construction. And the memoizer is constructed at `:931`, inside `inspectMutationGates`, which is downstream of root selection in `hook-dispatch.ts:201`. A resolver placed at the CLI entry gets no cache at all.

Net: **one** extra spawn per gated direct-write dispatch if the resolver runs inside `inspectMutationGates` and shares `dispatchGit`; more than that if it runs at the CLI entry. Put it inside the dispatch.

**The harder problem.** `worktreePath()` returns `string` and swallows failure: `git.ts:156-159` returns `resolve(projectRoot)` whenever git exits non-zero. I confirmed the failure is reachable -- `git -C <nonexistent> rev-parse --show-toplevel` exits 128, and `defaultGitRunner` maps a Node-level spawn `ENOENT` (which a nonexistent `cwd` produces) to `code: 127` with the message "git executable not found on PATH" (`git.ts:39-41`), conflating a missing directory with a missing binary. A `Write` that creates a file in a directory that does not exist yet is the common case for a new xBRIEF or a new module. So the resolver would silently fall back to the wrong root, reproducing the exact defect with no signal, and AC3 could never fire because it cannot distinguish "resolved to the payload root" from "failed and defaulted to the payload root."

**Disposition consequence.** AC3 is not implementable on `worktreePath()` as written. It needs a sibling that returns `string | null`, plus a walk-up to the nearest existing ancestor directory before spawning. Add that to the acceptance list.

### 9. `footnote` -- sequencing against #3599: no semantic collision

#3599 changes what a lease *means* inside `occupancy.ts` (age cap, refresh discrimination). This issue changes which file `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` is pointed at, from `dispatcher.ts`. `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate`'s signature (`occupancy.ts:421-442`) is untouched by either. I see no semantic collision. The only interaction worth a line: re-pointing multiplies the number of live lease files by the number of worktrees, so an absolute age cap will now expire many short-lived per-worktree leases rather than one long-lived primary lease. That is the intended direction, but it changes the population #3599 was tuned against.

`fixtures/cases.ts` has zero Codex or Claude direct-write cases (all five non-Cursor cases are Shell), and zero cases carrying a nested execution directory. ## Road not taken

I considered recommending a zero-spawn fix: reorder `hookPayloadRootCandidates` so `cwd` outranks `workspace_roots`. The hook child's `process.cwd()` is already the fallback (`hook-dispatch.ts:199-202`), and for a Codex agent running inside a worktree it is plausibly the worktree. I rejected it. On Cursor, payload `cwd` is the workspace root -- `cases.ts:228` shows `workspace_roots` and `cwd` set to the same value -- so the reorder is a no-op on the host with the richest payload, and on hosts where it does bite it substitutes an unverified field for a wrong one without any containment check. It trades a deterministic wrong answer for a host-dependent one.

## Steelman

The strongest case against my verdict: the diagnosis is right, the mechanism (`--show-toplevel`) demonstrably works, and everything I have raised is an implementation detail that a careful patch handles. I tested that. `git -C <linked-worktree> rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns the linked worktree, not the primary, despite the worktree being a valid subpath of the primary -- so the nesting concern the envelope raised does **not** break it. If AC1 were scoped to direct writes, AC3 landed in the same commit with a `--git-common-dir` containment test, and ritual moved with occupancy, the target would survive.

What would flip my verdict to SURVIVED: an amended acceptance list that (a) drops or conditions the execution-directory limb, (b) binds AC1 and AC3 into one commit, (c) names occupancy-plus-ritual as an atomic seam and explicitly pins authz and the audit trail to the payload root, and (d) replaces `worktreePath()` with a failure-expressing resolver. Those are four edits to the issue, not a different design.

## Minimal correct first change

One commit, direct writes only:

1. In `inspectMutationGates`, name two roots. Keep `payloadRoot = resolve(input.projectRoot)` for authz (`:780`), the authz audit (`:686`), `runningInsideDeftRepo` (`:1488`), the `.deft-directive-disable` probe, and `deny()`.
2. Compute `effectiveRoot` once, from the git toplevel of the nearest existing ancestor of `hookWriteTargetPath(input.payload)` -- available at `:937`, before occupancy -- through the memoized runner already built at `:931`, using a `string | null` resolver so failure is visible.
3. Admit `effectiveRoot` only when its `rev-parse --git-common-dir` equals `payloadRoot`'s. Otherwise fall back to `payloadRoot`. This is one comparison and it is simultaneously the linked-worktree admission, the foreign-repository refusal, and AC3's cross-worktree detector.
4. Use `effectiveRoot` for `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` (`:1011`, `:1115`) **and** `verifySessionRitual` (`:988`) -- both or neither.
5. Carry `effectiveRoot` into the decision's `projectRoot` and into every deny message, so an operator can see which tree was judged.

Scope, the `file_scope` relativization, and the assist-scratch reclassification are a deliberate second commit. Do not bundle them, and do not land step 4 as two commits.

## Verified synthesis -- BROKEN 3/3, and two of my own premises went with it

Three critics, presumption-refutation. Deposits 5434003949, 5434012950, 5434038821 (the last posted by me on the critic's behalf -- see the provenance note at the end). The diagnosis in the issue body holds. The **remedy** does not, in the specific shape the acceptance list describes.

### What I got wrong in the write-back

**1. I told all three critics that shell is occupancy-gated. It is not.**

I wrote that `dispatcher.ts` exempts only `isSpawnTool`, so `Bash`/`Shell` goes through the same gate. Shell reaches `inspectMutationGates` only via `decideShellDestFormsThenRuntimeAuthority` (`:1310`), inside `if (command !== null && destFormsEnforced)`, and `destFormsEnforced` requires `shellDestForms === "enforce"` (`:1308-1309`). The default is `"off"` (`runtime-authority.ts:73`) and this repo does not set it.

**Occupancy gates exactly one tool family today: direct writes.** All three critics caught this independently. It was my error and it shaped the `audit:shell-path` marker I handed them.

**2. My `:616` cite was wrong.** `hookWriteTargetPath` at `:616` sits inside `runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite`, which has three call sites -- `:948`, `:1168`, `:1269`. The latter two run *after* occupancy at `:1011`; `:948` runs before it but sits in the assist-scratch branch that returns at `:950-963` and never reaches the gate. So `:616` runs after occupancy on every path that actually evaluates a lease. **The correct pre-occupancy cite is `:937`.**

The claim it supported -- that the information is already in hand -- survives on the corrected cite.

### The execution-directory limb has no payload to stand on

Unanimous, and measured. No supported host sends a nested execution directory on a shell payload: all six Shell fixtures in `cases.ts` carry only `tool_input.command`, and none carries any of the four fields `LIFECYCLE_EXECUTION_DIRECTORY_FIELDS` reads. Where Cursor does send `cwd`, it equals `workspace_roots` -- byte-identical to the root the defect already picks. And `lifecycleExecutionRootCheck` returns `aligned: true` when the fields are absent, so the limb inherits a check that passes by default on missing input.

Implementing it produces a resolver that finds nothing on Codex and Claude, and the wrong answer on Cursor.

### The shape that survives: two roots, not one swap

Convergent across all three.

**Re-point to the mutation root** (git toplevel of the write target): occupancy, ritual, active scope, and every `toProjectRelativePosix`. The `file_scope` fence expects `packages/core/...`, not `.deft-scratch/worktrees/b3599/packages/core/...`.

**Pin explicitly to the payload root**: authz grant scoping (`:780` -> `authz/evaluate.ts:124-126` is an exact string match; re-pointing breaks every live UAT grant), the authz audit trail (`:686`, which would shard one repository-global evidence file into per-worktree files deleted with their worktree), the `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch (`:1545-1551`, untracked and therefore absent from linked worktrees -- re-pointing silently re-arms enforcement for an operator who believes Directive is off), and the #2885 outside-root carve-out.

### Four findings that change the acceptance list

**Occupancy and ritual are one atomic seam.** They are cross-compared at `:1058-1087` and `:1139-1151`. Move one and not the other and every worktree write denies `occupancy-ritual-mismatch`, with remediation no single `session:start` can satisfy, because `.deft/` is gitignored and the two files live in different trees. That is strictly worse than today, where the failure is at least actionable.

**AC1 without AC3 fails open.** Measured: `isOutsideProjectRootWrite(worktree, primaryFile)` is `true`, and `:1201-1202` skips the entire scope deny for outside-root writes. So in the window after AC1 and before AC3, cross-worktree writes are *less* gated than now. They are one commit, not two checkboxes.

**Target-toplevel resolution is an authority-selection primitive.** `worktreePath()` has no containment check, so an absolute path into a different repository on the same disk relocates occupancy, ritual, runtime authority, active scope, and the audit trail into that repository. The file path is attacker-influenceable. The remedy is one comparison: accept the resolved toplevel only when its `rev-parse --git-common-dir` matches the payload root's -- which is simultaneously the linked-worktree admission test, the foreign-repo refusal, and AC3's detector.

**`worktreePath()` cannot express the failure AC3 needs.** It returns `resolve(projectRoot)` on any non-zero exit, and a nonexistent `cwd` is mapped to "git executable not found on PATH". A write creating a file in a not-yet-existing directory is the common case. So the resolver would silently fall back to the wrong root, and AC3 could never distinguish that from success. It needs a `string | null` sibling plus a walk-up to the nearest existing ancestor.

### One finding that corrects a different issue

The `audit:ambiguity-remedy` marker I wrote asserted that #3779's ordering makes the occupancy denial's printed remedy unrunnable. **At default policy that does not hold.** `occupancy:steal` and `occupancy:release` arrive as Shell, match none of the four dest-forms, never enter `inspectMutationGates`, and reach `inspectExactLifecycleCommand` where both verbs are recognised. The recovery command is not blocked by the occupancy gate.

**#3779 needs re-derivation.** Its ordering claim was mine, from a code-path trace I filed without runtime verification, and I propagated it into this envelope. The real ambiguity trap is elsewhere: `lifecycleExecutionRootCheck` denies with "Run the lifecycle command from the hook project root" without naming the root, and for a genuine two-worktree span no single directory satisfies it. Any AC3 message must interpolate both concrete paths.

### Cost, reconciled rather than refuted

A critic measured git spawn at **37ms** unloaded and serial, against the 2.2s p50 in #3737. Both are right: that figure was a loaded N-agent measurement. The marginal spawn is cheap at rest and expensive exactly when a swarm is running. The existing memoizer keys on the *selected* root, so resolving the target's directory is a guaranteed miss -- one extra spawn per gated direct write if the resolver sits inside `inspectMutationGates`, more if it sits at the CLI entry.

### An unbudgeted consequence nobody had noted

Swarm worktrees live under `.deft-scratch/`, which is an assist-scratch prefix. Measured: **every file in every linked worktree is currently an allowlisted assist-scratch path**, so under assist or ephemeral posture those writes skip ritual, occupancy, and scope entirely today. Re-pointing closes that channel -- correct, but it is a new denial class for every assist-posture worktree agent, and it compounds with the ritual seam above. Land it deliberately with a migration note. It also suggests the placement of real product worktrees under a scratch-path fence deserves its own issue.

### Disposition

Recutting the acceptance list to: drop the execution-directory limb; bind AC1 and AC3 into one commit; name occupancy-plus-ritual as atomic and pin authz, the audit trail, and the kill-switch to the payload root; replace `worktreePath()` with a failure-expressing resolver; and add the `--git-common-dir` containment test. Scope, relativisation, and the assist-scratch reclassification become a deliberate second commit.

Not build-ready until recut. Chip stays `mechanism-shaped`.
